author: Allen Clayton
title: Bells Across America ring out in Morgantown for Constitution Week - NewsBreak
text:
By Allen Clayton ,
1 hours ago
MORGANTOWN, W.Va. (WBOY) — The sound of bells will echo across Morgantown this week as part of Bells Across America, a national tradition honoring the signing of the U.S. Constitution.
On Wednesday, Sept. 17, at 4 p.m., the bell in the Monongalia County Courthouse tower chimed, joining communities across the country in marking the anniversary of the Constitution’s signing in 1787. Local chapters of the Daughters of the American Revolution (DAR) invited residents to gather at the courthouse at 3:50 p.m. to take part in the event.
Participants were encouraged to bring their own bells to ring for one minute alongside the courthouse bell.
“It is very important that we remember the Constitution. I think if we look at what Canada and Europe are going through right now, we are blessed to have to have the constitution. We have free speech, they don’t,” Regent of the Woodburn Chapter of the DAR Joan Gibson said. “If you don’t have that strong constitution, which we have and the Bill of Rights, you don’t have rights you have privileges granted by a government.”
The nationwide bell ringing commemorates Sept. 17, 1787, when church bells rang out in Philadelphia to celebrate the signing of the Constitution.
Funding withheld for several student assistance programs in West Virginia Constitution Week is celebrated annually from Sept. 17–23 to highlight the importance of the nation’s founding document. The observance was established in 1956, after DAR petitioned Congress to set aside the week for nationwide recognition. President Dwight D. Eisenhower signed the resolution into law.
“When they signed the Constitution, they stepped out of Constitution Hall and said that it was signed, and the church bells rang out to let us know that we had the freedom. So, it’s something that we need to do every year to remind us how important the Constitution is to us,” Regent of Elizabeth Ludington Hagans-Colonel John Evans Chapter of the DAR Brenda Fisher said. “It’s important to know that we still have the Constitution; it’s such an important document in our lives.”
The week serves as a reminder of the Constitution’s role in protecting citizens’ liberties and freedoms , while also emphasizing the responsibility Americans share in defending those rights. Its goals include:
Encouraging study of the Constitution and its history. Emphasizing the duty of citizens to protect and uphold the Constitution. Highlighting the Constitution as the foundation of America’s heritage and way of life. The DAR, which also built Constitution Hall in Washington, D.C. in 1929, has continued to lead efforts to honor and preserve the document’s legacy.
Constitution Week offers communities a chance to reflect on the freedoms established more than two centuries ago and to celebrate the resilience of the American system of government.
